facts.fact: The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights said on 21 July 2026 that the e-Justice platform, developed by Malian teams, is about to launch, first for online nationality certificates and criminal records, with a second phase extending it to digital management of judicial files.

systems.owner: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights
systems.tiers: Bamako Court of Appeal staff trained as users

facts.fact: UNDP, with Dutch support, handed Mali's Ministry of Justice laptops, tablets and modems worth USD 493,193 on 5 November 2026 to equip the operationalisation of its e-justice platform.

systems.owner: Ministere de la Justice et des Droits de l'Homme

facts.fact: Justice Minister Mamoudou Kassogue said on 5 November 2026 that the ministry is operationalising a national e-justice platform whose first services are digital criminal-record extracts and nationality certificates, with later features to cover case processing.

systems.owner: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights

systems.platform: digital criminal record and nationality certificate

note: A citizen e-service for criminal records and nationality certificates, not a court case management system.

facts.fact: The justice minister said on 10 February 2026 that a pilot phase of the integrated judicial case-management system is under way, with eight courts already interconnected and two more to follow.

note: Filing, hearing calendars and online verdicts are announced as coming; the digitised payments are not court case management.
